title: French Chocolate Mousse
subtitle: Classic mousse made with just dark chocolate and eggs
excerpt: The simplest and best chocolate mousse. Just eggs and chocolate. No cream, no additives. It sets to a dark, intense foam that tastes exactly like what it is.
sourceNotes: Classic French dessert, known in France as mousse au chocolat.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made up to 24 hours ahead and kept chilled.

content.text: This serves 4 and takes about 25 minutes plus at least 3 hours chilling. The key thing to watch is folding in the egg whites: you need to keep the air you whipped in. Use a large metal spoon and fold in three additions, cutting down through the centre and sweeping up the sides.
Use the best dark chocolate you can find, at least 70% cocoa solids. This is all the flavour in the dish and cheap chocolate will produce a flat, sweet result.
Melt the chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water. Stir until smooth, then remove from heat and leave to cool for 5 minutes.
Beat the egg yolks and sugar together until pale. Stir into the cooled chocolate mixture.
In a clean, dry bowl, whisk the egg whites with a pinch of salt until they form stiff peaks.
Add a large spoonful of white to the chocolate mixture and stir in to loosen it.
Fold in the remaining egg whites in two more additions, using a large metal spoon. Work gently and stop as soon as no white streaks remain.
Divide between 4 cups or glasses. Cover and chill for at least 3 hours until set.

items.symptom: Mousse is dense and heavy rather than airy
items.cause: Egg whites were overmixed into the chocolate rather than folded
items.fix: Fold very gently with a cutting motion, stopping the moment the mixture is combined

items.symptom: Chocolate mixture seized when the eggs were added
items.cause: Chocolate was still too hot when the yolks were stirred in
items.fix: Let chocolate cool for at least 5 minutes - it should be warm but not hot to the touch

items.symptom: Mousse has not set after 3 hours
items.cause: Not enough air in the egg whites or fridge too warm
items.fix: Egg whites must be at stiff peaks before folding, and the fridge should be at 4C or below

content.text: Mousse au chocolat is a fixture of the French home table and has been since the 18th century when chocolate became widely available in Europe. The classic version uses only eggs and chocolate, with no cream added. It appears on bistro menus across France, usually served simply in a pot or small glass. Its simplicity is the point: the quality of the chocolate is given nowhere to hide.
